questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the matrix $F$ given below?

- $det(F)=0$
- $F$ is a singular matrix
- $det(F)=-2$

$$
F=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 7 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that a square matrix is singular if its determinant is equal to $0.$

Using the formula, we take the alternating sum of the entries in the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(F) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 7 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =0|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 7 & 8\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 6 & 8\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ 6 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-1(24-30)+2(21-24) \\  & =0-1\cdot (-6)+2\cdot (-3) \\  & =6-6 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $det(F)=0$, the matrix is singular. 

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.

questions.problem: Given that the determinant of  $[\begin{aligned}1 & n & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$ is $-6$, find the value of $n.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & n & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|-n|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+0|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4-n\cdot 2+0 \\  & =4-2n\end{aligned}
$$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $-6,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}4-2n & =-6 \\ -2n & =-10 \\ n & =5\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the matrix $M$ given below?

- $M$ is a singular matrix
- $det(M)=1$
- $det(M)=0$

 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that a square matrix is singular if its determinant is equal to $0.$

Using the formula, we take the alternating sum of the entries in the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-4-12)+2(-2+6)+1(4+4) \\  & =1\cdot (-16)+2\cdot 4+1\cdot 8 \\  & =-16+8+8 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $det(M)=0$, the matrix is singular. 

Therefore, only statements I and III are true.

questions.problem:
Given that the determinant of
$[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & m \\ m & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]$
is $-29$, find all the possible values of $m.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $m:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & m \\ m & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-6|\begin{aligned}m & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+m|\begin{aligned}m & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(3-0)-6(m-0)+m(m-6) \\  & =3-6m+{m}^{2}-6m \\  & ={m}^{2}-12m+3\end{aligned}
$$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $-29,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}^{2}-12m+3 & =-29 \\ {m}^{2}-12m+32 & =0 \\ m & =\frac{-(-12)\pm \sqrt{{12}^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 32}}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{12\pm 4}{2} \\  & =6\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $m=4$ and $m=8.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Determinant of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula, we take the alternating sum of the entries in the top row of the matrix, multiplied by their respective minors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 & 6 \\ 2 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}| & =5|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}-1 & 6 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =5(4\cdot 1-6\cdot (-3))+2((-1)(1)-6\cdot 2)+3((-1)(-3)-4\cdot 2) \\  & =5(4+18)+2(-1-12)+3(3-8) \\  & =5(22)+2(-13)+3(-5) \\  & =110-26-15 \\  & =69\end{aligned}
$$
